newsitem.title: USA: Occidental buys three chemical producers.
newsitem.headline: Occidental buys three chemical producers.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp. said Tuesday it acquired three speciality chemical producers in separate deals for a total of about $146 million.

The acquisitions are part of the Los Angeles-based oil company's strategy to grow its speciality chemicals businesses from an annual earnings base of $65 million in 1995 to $250 million annually by the year 2000, it said.
About $127 million will be paid in shares of Occidental common stock, it said.

Laurel Industries, Inc., acquired from private investors, is North America's largest producer of antimony oxide at its LaPorte, Texas, facility. Antimony oxide is used in the manufacture of plastic resins and as a flame retardant in plastics.
Natural Gas Odorizing, purchased from Helmerich & Payne, is the nation's leading producer of mercaptan-based warning agents for use in natural gas and propane from its single plant in Baytown, Texas.
A plant in Augusta, Ga., purchased from Power Silicates Manufacturing, Inc., produces sodium silicates used to make soap, detergents and paper.
The acquisitions will immediately boost Occidental's earnings and cash flow, the company said.
Its stock rose 62.5 cents to $23.875 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
